To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the alloying elements, especially Si, have a significant influence on the reaction between Al melt and Ti powders, and the microstructures of the resulting reinforcements during heating of powder compact at 993 K. This
alloying elements have significant effects on the formation of core-shell structured Ti reinforcement particles during heating of Al–Ti powder compacts.
the alloying elements, including Si, Cu, and Mg, have a positive influence on the formation of core-shell-structured reinforcing particles during heating of Al–Ti powder compacts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of core-shell-structured reinforcements during heating of Al–Ti powder compacts.
the effect of alloying elements on the formation of core-shell-structured reinforcing particles during heating of Al–Ti powder compacts.
the effect of alloying elements on the reaction between Al melt and Ti powders and the formation of core-shell-structured reinforcing particles during heating of powder compact.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the formation of core-shell structured reinforcing particles was closely related to the reaction rate, the product phase constituents and the microstructure characteristics of the reaction products, which were all affected by the alloying elements.

the alloying elements had different effects on the formation of core-shell-structured reinforcing particles during heating of Al–Ti powder compacts, and Si element could promote the formation of core–shell–structured Ti@compoundp reinforced Al matrix composite.

Si was the optimal element for obtaining core-shell-structured reinforcing particles in Al–Ti–X systems (X = Si, Cu, and Mg), and the Al–Ti system was the optimal alloy for obtaining core-shell structured Ti particles in Al–X–Ti (X = Si and Mg) systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the alloying elements had a significant effect on the formation of core-shell-structured particles during the heating process of the powder compacts, which was helpful for the formation of the core-shell-structured reinforcements in the semis solid Al matrix.
the alloying element should be selected from the elements that can promote the formation of Al3Ti phase, and the alloying element with high affinity for Ti should be avoided.

the alloying elements could affect the formation of the reinforcing particles during heating and in the semis solid state, but the effect on the reaction was more obvious than that in the semisoid state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of core-shell-structured reinforcing particles in the semis solid state was more difficult than that in the solid state.
the addition of Si is an effective way to obtain the core-shell-structured reinforcements with thick and compact reaction shells.

alloying elements play important roles in the microstructural evolution of the reinforcements during heating of powder compact and in the microstructure of reinforcements in the corresponding semisolids, which should be paid more attention when designing core-shell-structured reinforcing particles in the future.
